applicant_utility.summary: This is a short, part-funded clinical observership for neurologists in residency or within five years of their latest neurology degree, paying EUR 425 per week for a 6-12 week stay at an approved EAN host department outside your home country. The written justification is the main differentiator: EAN states that explaining the gains expected in the context of your usual practice is a major rating factor. Secure both an approved host and an active EAN membership well before the 31 October 2026 cutoff, because membership approval alone can take up to 10 working days.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Neurologists in residency or recently qualified who want a 6-12 week observership at a European centre of expertise and can name a specific technique, service structure or practice to observe.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your EAN RRFS or Full membership is active; if you still need to join, apply at least 3 weeks before 31 October 2026 because approval can take up to 10 working days
Select a host from the published 2027/2028 approved department list and obtain the signed host acceptance form naming a supervisor who will have at least weekly direct contact
Draft the justification around your own usual practice and the concrete gains expected, plus a reasoned request for the number of weeks, since both are explicitly rated
Collect two recommendation letters, each from a different individual neurologist
Gather evidence of at least 2 years of clinical neurology training together with a declaration of the hospital where the training took place
Retain all original documents until the outcome is notified, as fresh copies may be requested
common_rejection_risks: A generic justification that never links the host department's specific expertise to gains in your own practice
Requesting weeks without reasoning on the length of the stay
Hosting department missing from the approved 2027/2028 list
Inactive or still-pending EAN membership at the deadline
Choosing a host inside your own country, when the stay must be outside your country of residence
Exceeding the quota for Corresponding Institutional Member or low and lower-middle income sub-Saharan African countries (maximum 10% and up to two per country)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, meals and local transport beyond the EUR 425 weekly grant; any travel above the EUR 300 cap, which is reimbursed only after the fellowship ends; visa, insurance, EAN membership fees and any congress costs are not stated as covered.
document_audit: The host acceptance form must name a supervisor expected to have at least weekly direct contact during the stay
Training evidence must prove a minimum of 2 years of clinical neurology experience and include a hospital declaration
Two separate recommendation letters from two individual neurologists are required - a single joint letter will not satisfy this
The application form is visible in MyEAN only between 1 August and 31 October 2026, so late registrations cannot even see it
alerts: Applications close 31 October 2026 and the form is invisible outside the 1 August - 31 October window
EAN membership applications can take up to 10 working days - submit at least 3 weeks before the deadline
If your preferred host is not on the approved list, it must submit a department access form by 15 September 2026 to be considered for the 2027 round
Results are only communicated by the end of December 2026, so do not commit to travel or leave dates before then
Travel money is reimbursed only after the stay, against the final report, mentor confirmation and evaluation forms
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Log into MyEAN, open the members-only application hub link, complete the online form with the eligibility declaration, and upload the host acceptance form, training evidence and two recommendation letters before 31 October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a EUR 2,000 monthly fellowship letting European neurologists run 6-12 months of basic, clinical or applied neuroscience research at an academic department outside their home country, with up to EUR 500 in travel. The 2027 round closed on 31 August 2026 and outcomes are due by the end of November 2026, so the next realistic target is the following annual window. Feasibility, methods, the host department, your CV and the overall impression carry the most weight, so a tightly scoped project anchored at a strong department beats an ambitious but vague abstract.
applicant_utility.best_fit: European neurologists with an active EAN RRFS or Full membership who need dedicated research time abroad en route to a higher degree, a grant application or a first peer-reviewed publication.
application_readiness_checklist: Obtain the acceptance letter from the chair of the host institution before applying, including the proposed mentor's short CV and bibliography
Write the project description with the five required sections - background, aims, methods, timetable, references - and make feasibility and the requested months explicitly match
Complete the official EAN CV form including the full publications list instead of a free-format CV
Secure the home department chair's recommendation using EAN's own form, plus a second recommendation letter from another neurologist
Prepare the document confirming your neurology training and its duration in English
Verify your EAN RRFS or Full membership is active; approval can take up to 10 working days
common_rejection_risks: A project over-scoped for the time requested, since feasibility is one of the weighted scores
A weak host department or supervisor, which two of the nine scores directly cover
A host institution inside your own country, when the research must be outside your country of residence
An acceptance letter from a supervisor instead of the chair of the host institution, or one missing the mentor's CV and bibliography
Submitting anything on paper or by e-mail - only the online application form is accepted
Applications that cannot show value beyond the training already available in your own country or institution
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the EUR 2,000 monthly allowance; any travel above the EUR 500 cap, reimbursed only after the fellowship ends; visa, insurance, university or bench fees and EAN membership costs are not stated as covered.
document_audit: The acceptance letter must come from the chair of the host institution and include the mentor's short CV and bibliography
The training confirmation document must be in English
The home-department recommendation uses EAN's preset form, not a free letter from the chair
Original documents or fresh copies may be requested after submission, so keep everything until the outcome is notified
alerts: The 2027 window closed on 31 August 2026; EAN presents the fellowship as annual, so expect roughly a June-August opening in the next cycle
Notifications only arrive by the end of November 2026, so avoid signing competing commitments before then
Successful fellowships are valid retroactively from 1 September 2026 if the stay started earlier
Full members must be within 5 years of their latest neurology degree; RRFS members need more than 2 years of residency training at the time of the event
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the EAN online application form during the annual window, uploading the EAN CV form, English training confirmation, project description, home-department chair recommendation, second neurologist recommendation and the host chair's acceptance letter.
